subject: Human Evolution
title: The Achilles Tendon
description: A quick win: understand The Achilles Tendon.

hook.text: Chimps barely have an Achilles tendon. Ours is massive—and it exists solely because we run.

buildup.text: The tendon acts like a rubber band, storing energy when the foot lands and releasing it at push-off.

discovery.text: Walking doesn't need much elastic recoil. The Achilles tendon's spring function only matters at speed.

twist.text: Australopithecus lacked a modern Achilles tendon. It appeared with Homo—suggesting running drove its evolution.

climax.text: This one tendon saves about 35% of the energy cost of running—without it, distance running is impossible.

punchline.text: One tendon made us marathon runners.

quiz.question: What function does the Achilles tendon serve during running?
